quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar, how does stopping compare to riding without a sidecar?

options.text: Stopping will be easier.
Stopping will take longer.
You cannot stop.
Stopping is about the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping will take longer.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle. Extra weight means you need more braking force to stop. Stopping takes longer downhill than on flat ground.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective riding gear?

options.text: A leather jacket
Boots that cover your ankles
Hearing protection
Pants made of soft material

questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of soft material
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a leather jacket, leather pants, boots that cover your ankles, and hearing protection. Soft material does not protect you in a crash.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When passing another vehicle
When you will slow down suddenly
When there is a stop sign ahead
When your signals do not work

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly
questions.explanation: A motorcycle has only one brake light, which is not as noticeable as a car's two larger brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps other drivers notice when you slow down quickly.

questions.question: Motorists entering a highway from the right may not see your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Flash your lights.
Move to the left side of your lane to make room.
Move into another lane if you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane if you can.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of room to vehicles entering the highway. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if possible. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give them safe entry room.

questions.question: What should you do when turning on a motorcycle?

options.text: Keep your eyes focused close to the front of the motorcycle.
Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.
Increase your speed before the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: How can you discourage other drivers from sharing your lane?

options.text: By giving dirty looks to other drivers
By riding in the center of the lane
By riding in the left portion of the lane
By riding in a zigzag pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the center of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane. This leaves less space on both sides and makes it harder for other drivers to try to share the lane with you.

questions.question: What should a face shield do?

options.text: Allow a clear view to both sides
Prevent all air from passing through it
Be tight enough to prevent glasses from fitting under it
Not fasten too tightly

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a clear view to both sides
questions.explanation: A good face shield should have no scratches, resist penetration, provide clear views to both sides, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and fit room for glasses if needed.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders ride in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group
Just behind the lead rider
At the back of the group
Anywhere in the group

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders behind them can watch and help if needed.

questions.question: When a motorcycle leans while turning, what happens to braking traction?

options.text: The amount of traction available for braking is reduced.
The amount of traction available for braking is increased.
The brakes work more smoothly than usual.
The motorcycle has more stability than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: The amount of traction available for braking is reduced.
questions.explanation: When your motorcycle leans, there is less traction for braking. It is best to brake before you enter a turn, not while turning.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: Always the right side of the lane
Always the center of the lane
Always the left side of the lane
It changes based on road, weather, and traffic conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: It changes based on road, weather, and traffic conditions
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position at all times. Change your lane position based on the road, weather, and traffic around you.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Means that they see you.
Guarantees that they will yield to you.
Does not mean that they see you.
Is not worth the effort.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean that they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know that a driver will yield. A driver can look directly at you and still not notice you.

questions.question: What happens if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jump forward and the rear tire may slide.
The horn may go off.
Your motorcycle may jump forward and the front tire may slide.
Your motorcycle may jump forward and a warning light will turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jump forward and the rear tire may slide.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, your motorcycle may jump forward and the rear tire may slide. This causes you to lose control. Slow down before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Let them ride.
Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
Push their bike over.
Get other friends to convince them not to ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to convince them not to ride.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone to ride if they have been drinking. Do everything you can to stop them. Ask other friends to help you talk them out of riding.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Only use your mirrors to see all around you.
Point in the direction you are changing lanes.
Speed up to pass other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Do not only rely on your mirrors.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that show rules, like speed limits, are rectangular with white background and black letters. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should not rely only on mirrors because:

options.text: Motorcycle mirrors are smaller than car mirrors, so you cannot see as much.
Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars.
Mirrors are never accurate.
Mirrors take your eyes off the road and should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. You cannot rely only on mirrors to see what is behind you. Check over your shoulder frequently.

questions.question: The best source of information for your motorcycle is:

options.text: The owner's manual.
A general book about motorcycles.
Someone who rides a different motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle. It has information specific to your motorcycle.

questions.question: Riding alongside another rider:

options.text: Allows you to use more of the road.
Should be avoided because it limits your escape routes.
Allows you to talk with each other.
Makes it easier for other drivers to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be avoided because it limits your escape routes.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another motorcyclist. It limits the escape routes for both of you if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Always use both brakes.
Only use the front brake.
Only use the rear brake on wet pavement.
Only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter what the road conditions are.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Give you a good view of the shoulder.
Give you a poor view of road hazards.
Invite other riders to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and be seen by them. Do not stay in another driver's blind spot for a long time.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chance of crashing?

options.text: Do not use your turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Watch only five feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Always be ready to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your turn signals, brake light, and proper lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle. Look ahead, behind, and beside your vehicle. Be ready to avoid sudden hazards.

questions.question: How can you be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Turn your headlight off.
Ride with your headlight on.
Make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see you at an intersection is to ride with your headlight on. Keep your headlight on whenever your motorcycle is running.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help reduce your chance of crashing?

options.text: Be visible by wearing proper clothing and using your headlight.
Use your turn signals and brake light to show your intentions.
Look for hazards in your path.
Hope other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: To prevent crashes, be visible to other drivers, communicate your moves, and keep space around you. Look for and avoid hazards. Be ready to react to anything that happens. Do not rely on hoping others see you.

questions.question: Your motorcycle starts to weave over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Brake suddenly.
Steer in a weaving pattern.
Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Move to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles may weave over rain grooves or bridge gratings, but this is usually safe. If your motorcycle weaves, stay relaxed and go straight at a steady speed. Weaving side to side will only make it more dangerous.

questions.question: What is true about rain suits?

options.text: They should not be used.
They should not balloon when riding.
They are not needed because motorcycles should not be ridden in rain.
They should tear easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should not balloon when riding.
questions.explanation: Good quality motorcycle rain suits resist tearing and ballooning when you ride at high speeds.
